studies.Title: Dietary patterns and risk of advanced prostate cancer: a principal component analysis in Uruguay.
studies.Reference: Dietary patterns and risk of advanced prostate cancer: a principal component analysis in Uruguay.
studies.Population: Uruguayan men, including newly diagnosed advanced prostate cancer cases and hospitalized controls
studies.comparison_type: High quartile versus low quartile of Western diet

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: In order to explore the role of broader eating patterns in the etiology of prostate cancer, we conducted a principal components analysis among Uruguayan men. The study included 345 newly diagnosed cases of advanced prostate cancer and 690 hospitalized controls.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: The study included 345 newly diagnosed cases of advanced prostate cancer and 690 hospitalized controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Whereas the traditional and Western patterns were directly associated with risk of prostate cancer (OR for high quartile versus the low quartile of the Western diet was 2.35, 95% CI 1.44-3.85, p-value for trend < 0.0001), the prudent, drinker, and substituter patterns were not associated with risk of the disease.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: Whereas the traditional and Western patterns were directly associated with risk of prostate cancer (OR for high quartile versus the low quartile of the Western diet was 2.35, 95% CI 1.44-3.85, p-value for trend < 0.0001), the prudent, drinker, and substituter patterns were not associated with risk of the disease.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: high quartile versus the low quartile of the Western diet
extraction_supporting_text.design: The study included 345 newly diagnosed cases of advanced prostate cancer and 690 hospitalized controls.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: we conducted a principal components analysis among Uruguayan men

studies.Population: Men participating in the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study
studies.Reference: Dietary patterns and prostate cancer risk in Japanese: the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study (JPHC Study).
studies.Authors: Shin S, Saito E, Sawada N, Ishihara J, Takachi R, Nanri A, Shimazu T, Yamaji T, Iwasaki M, Sasazuki S, Inoue M, Tsugane S, JPHC Study Group
studies.Timing: Diet assessed in the 5-year follow-up survey; participants were followed from 1995–1998 through the end of 2012
studies.comparison_type: High versus low westernized dietary-pattern adherence; exact category definitions are not stated in the abstract.
studies.direction_original_comparison: High versus low westernized dietary-pattern adherence; exact category definitions are not stated in the abstract.
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire in the 5-year follow-up survey. Three major dietary patterns were derived using exploratory factors analysis: prudent, westernized, and traditional dietary patterns.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The westernized dietary pattern was associated with a higher risk of total prostate cancer (HR: 1.22; 95% CI 1.00-1.49; p trend = 0.021), localized cancer (HR: 1.24; 95% CI 0.97-1.57; p trend = 0.045), and advanced cancer (HR: 1.23; 95% CI 0.82-1.84; p trend = 0.233).
extraction_supporting_text.cases: A total of 43,469 men who participated in the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study were followed from 1995 to 1998 to the end of 2012, during which 1,156 cases of prostate cancer were newly identified.
